proofs.full_local_argument: Fix x in X and y in R^m. Set z=y*(x), d=||y-z||_2. The linked exact identity gives grad Phi(x)=h(x,z). Write A_y=A(x,y), H_y=H(x,y), b_y=f_y(x,y), a_y=f_x(x,y), and similarly with subscript z. Strong convexity gives ||H_y^-1||_2,||H_z^-1||_2<=1/mu_g. The exact identity H_y^-1-H_z^-1=H_y^-1(H_z-H_y)H_z^-1 implies ||H_y^-1-H_z^-1||_2<=L_gyy d/mu_g^2. Expand A_y H_y^-1 b_y-A_z H_z^-1 b_z as A_y H_y^-1(b_y-b_z)+(A_y-A_z)H_y^-1 b_z+A_z(H_y^-1-H_z^-1)b_z. The three terms have norms bounded respectively by (C_gxy L_fy/mu_g)d, (L_gxy C_fy/mu_g)d, and (C_gxy L_gyy C_fy/mu_g^2)d. Also ||a_y-a_z||_2<=L_fx d. Subtract the product difference from a_y-a_z and use the triangle inequality to obtain precisely C d. These estimates use induced matrix 2-norm and its action on Euclidean vectors. If source matrix regularity bounds are interpreted as Frobenius bounds, ||B||_2<=||B||_F supplies the same required upper bounds; the inverse-Hessian estimate here remains exclusively spectral. Since x,y were arbitrary, the stated quantifiers follow.

assumptions: n,m are positive finite integers. X is a nonempty closed convex subset of R^n. Lower minimization is over all R^m. f is C^1 and g is C^2 on an open neighborhood of X times R^m, explicitly stating the local smooth-extension interpretation for derivatives at boundary points.
Assumption 1(a): uniformly in x in X, f_x(x,.) and f_y(x,.) are Lipschitz in y with finite positive L_fx,L_fy.
Assumption 1(b): ||f_y(x,y)||_2<=C_fy uniformly on X times R^m, with finite C_fy>0.
Assumption 1(c): uniformly in y, f_y(.,y) is Lipschitz on X with finite positive barL_fy.
Assumption 2(a): g is continuously twice differentiable in (x,y).
Assumption 2(b): uniformly in x, g_y(x,.) is Lipschitz with finite positive L_g.
Assumption 2(c): g(x,.) is mu_g-strongly convex on R^m uniformly in x, mu_g>0; H>=mu_g I.
Assumption 2(d): uniformly in x, A(x,.) and H(x,.) are Lipschitz in y with finite positive L_gxy,L_gyy.

Assumption 2(f): uniformly in y, A(.,y) and H(.,y) are Lipschitz on X with finite positive barL_gxy,barL_gyy. All source standing conditions are retained, including x-regularity not needed by the local pointwise estimate.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Phi(x)=f(x,y*(x)), y*(x)=argmin_{y in R^m}g(x,y), A=g_xy, H=g_yy, and h(x,y)=f_x(x,y)-A(x,y)H(x,y)^-1 f_y(x,y). Vectors use Euclidean 2-norm; matrix constants in the local argument use induced 2-norm. Definition 1.1 does not explicitly distinguish induced matrix norm from Frobenius norm. Frobenius regularity upper bounds imply the operator upper bounds used here; no Frobenius inverse-Hessian bound is asserted.
statement.parameter_domains: n,m positive finite integers; all named constants finite and positive; mu_g>0.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every x in X and every y in R^m, deterministically; constants are uniform in the variables specified by the assumptions.

Source notation and the local conventions remain distinct. The local argument uses induced matrix 2-norm and does not assert ||H^-1||_F<=1/mu_g.
The bound applies to the exact implicit estimator. Inexact linear solves need a separate residual argument and resource accounting.
Pointwise bias does not establish an outer convergence rate or unrestricted Oracle Complexity.
